cards.kicker: Mexico City Grand Prix · Race · 71 laps
cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 27 on-track passes, 34 pit stops, 5 cars that never finished, 2 safety cars, 1 virtual safety car and a red flag that stopped the race.

cards.title: 30 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: Perez gained the most by the end of it, 6 places
cards.note: Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the race.

cards.title: 13 incidents looked at
cards.text: Every one of them logged by race control during the race.
bullets: Lap 1: Hamilton and Leclerc, an incident
4 ended in a penalty, 6 in no further action and 3 left for after the race

cards.title: Lawson starts P22. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 71 laps to make up ground from there.
cards.reveal: Somewhere in the points. The exact place comes at the flag.

cards.title: 13 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Piastri, Bortoleto, Hirakawa and 2 others lost 2 each, the most of anybody
cards.note: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty.

cards.title: Stroll is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 6 of 71, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P22 at the start of lap 5
Started P19
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Alonso is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 6 of 71, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P21 at the start of lap 5
Started P17

cards.title: Everybody slows down, nobody bunches up
cards.text: Every car is held to a delta time exactly where it is. The gaps freeze instead of vanishing, which is the whole difference from a real safety car.
bullets: Leclerc was leading when it was called
Hadjar took a stop under it
Lifted on lap 8
cards.note: A stop under a VSC costs less than one at racing speed, because everybody else is going slowly too. Cheaper, not free: the leader keeps his gap and the queue behind him keeps its shape.

cards.title: Track at 47°C at the start, falling to 34°C at the flag
cards.text: Track temperature changes how much grip the tyres find and how fast they wear. No rain was recorded during the race.

cards.title: Hadjar: 8 passes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Red Bull.
bullets: P7 on the grid, P9 at the flag
cards.note: Only moves made on track count, with the car ahead at racing speed.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Hamilton on lap 50, 1:19.268, in a Ferrari.

cards.title: Gasly and Hirakawa hit 361 km/h
cards.text: The trap reads one fixed point on the lap, so a car can go faster elsewhere. And the fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine

cards.title: 34 stops, and the busiest lap saw 4 of them
cards.text: Once one car stops, the cars around it have to answer.
bullets: Busiest single lap was 44, with 4 cars in
Shortest time in the pit lane: Hulkenberg, 21.9s
Longest: Hulkenberg, 34.5s
cards.note: Pit lane time runs from the entry line to the exit line, stop included.

cards.title: Antonelli ran one set for 43 laps
cards.text: The longest anybody stayed out on one set.
bullets: On the softs, lap 1 to lap 43
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane. And every lap you stretch is a set of tyres getting slower underneath you.

cards.title: Bottas is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 43 of 71, in a Cadillac.
bullets: P20 at the start of lap 42
Started P21

cards.title: Yellow flags out 6 times
cards.text: Race control waves a yellow for anything on or near the track that should not be there.
bullets: A yellow means slow down and do not overtake in that part of the track
Track sectors 3 and 4 saw 4 calls each, more than anywhere else

cards.title: The race was stopped
cards.text: A safety car first, then the red flag: everybody into the pit lane and a wait for the track to be made safe.
bullets: Verstappen was leading when it happened
Standing restart on lap 46
cards.note: Teams can change tyres while the cars wait, which rewrites the strategies on the grid.

cards.title: Lap 47: an incident between Hamilton and Verstappen at Turn 1. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and it lands on your desk. If one driver is to blame, what does he get? Same call the stewards had to make.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the race on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if there is no stop left. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards took no further action.

cards.title: 4 penalties handed out
cards.text: Given by the stewards during the race.
bullets: Leclerc: a 5s penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage
Russell: a 10s penalty for causing a collision
Perez: a 5s penalty for speeding in the pit lane
And 1 more
cards.note: A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left.

cards.title: Bearman is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 48 of 71, in a Haas.
bullets: P12 at the start of lap 47
Started P14

cards.title: Verstappen had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Hamilton: 1:19.268
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all race, in a Ferrari.
bullets: Set on lap 50 of 71, in the second half, with the car already lighter than at the start
It is worth no points: the bonus point for it was dropped after 2024

cards.title: One of these three does not see the chequered flag. Who?
cards.text: Nothing on the timing screens says it is coming.
cards.reveal: Lindblad, on lap 59 of 71. Race control had logged an incident involving Piastri and Lindblad at Turn 2.

cards.title: Hirakawa: 10 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the race, from lap 48 to lap 57, at racing speed.
bullets: 10 other drivers had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: Safety car with 12 laps left. You are leading. Box or stay out?
cards.text: The pack is about to bunch up behind you and a stop costs far less than usual, except that everybody behind can copy you and anyone who stays out may come out ahead.

choices.label: Box for fresh tyres
choices.sub: Grip for the restart, at the risk of track position

choices.label: Stay out and defend
choices.sub: Keep the lead on older tyres

outcomes.box: New rubber under a safety car is close to free. If the cars behind follow you in, the order holds. If they stay out, your gap has to cover the stop.
outcomes.stay: You keep the lead and restart on older tyres, with a queue of fresher cars in your mirrors and no gap to hide in.

cards.title: Every gap on track, erased
cards.text: The field bunches up behind the safety car, and whatever anybody had built is gone.
bullets: Verstappen was leading when it came out
He stayed out while Hirakawa, Hulkenberg and Perez stopped under it
Neutralised until lap 62
cards.note: A lead built over a long run was worth nothing at the restart, and whoever had fresher tyres underneath him suddenly had a race again.

cards.title: Lindblad is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 59 of 71, in a Racing Bulls car.
bullets: P7 at the start of lap 58
Started P8
Race control logged an incident with Piastri and Lindblad at Turn 2 on lap 59

cards.title: Lindblad was P7 a lap before his race ended on lap 59. Where does he finish if it had not?
cards.text: Nobody can answer this one for certain. You have his own lap times to go on and nothing else.
state: Slower than all of the eventual top five

choices.label: He keeps it in the points
He drops out of the points

cards.reveal: Our read from his own lap times, not a fact. He was lapping 1.18s a lap slower than the car that went on to win it, over the same laps. With 12 laps left, "he keeps it in the points" is the honest guess, and nobody gets to check. Race control had logged an incident involving Piastri and Lindblad on lap 59.

cards.title: Gasly went the other way: 8 places lost
cards.text: Qualifying promised one thing and the race delivered another.
bullets: P9 on the grid, P17 at the flag
2 stops when most of the field made 1
Qualifying rewards whoever can put one lap together. A race asks for 71 of them

cards.title: Lawson: P22 on the grid, P7 at the flag
cards.text: 15 places gained.
bullets: 5 on-track passes along the way
5 cars that started ahead of him retired

cards.title: How far behind was Hamilton at the flag?
cards.text: 71 laps, 1 hour 41 minutes of racing. Put a number on the gap to the winner.
cards.reveal: 0.799 seconds after 71 laps. A trip down the pit lane took about 23s today, which is 29 times this gap.

cards.title: Verstappen wins it
cards.text: P1 Verstappen · P2 Hamilton · P3 Antonelli.
bullets: After 71 laps, Hamilton crossed the line 0.799s behind
cards.note: Less than the time it takes to read this sentence.
